patient.chief_complaint: Progressive behavioral changes, disinhibition, impaired judgment — 15 months; referred from psychiatry after inadequate antidepressant response
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. J is a 55-year-old clinical social worker with HIV (undetectable viral load on Biktarvy for 8 years), hypertension, and depression who is referred from her psychiatrist for neurological evaluation. She presents with her close friend of 20 years, who serves as the primary informant. Her psychiatrist referred her after 18 months of progressive behavioral and personality changes that have not responded to two antidepressant trials (escitalopram and now sertraline at 150 mg). Her friend describes a 15-month history of progressive behavioral changes that are markedly different from her previously known depressive episodes. She has become impulsive — she gave away her laptop to a stranger on the street, claiming he 'needed it more.' She made sexually inappropriate comments to a colleague at work, leading to an HR complaint, which she dismissed entirely. She now follows a rigid daily schedule of her own design and becomes agitated when anything deviates from it. She has developed a habit of watching the same nature documentary series every evening, having watched each episode more than 30 times. She shows no empathy toward clients, which her supervisor noted in an incident report — she was asking detailed questions about clients' trauma histories in front of other staff. She is on medical leave from work. She has no insight into these changes. Her HIV is well-controlled with Biktarvy — CD4 count 680 cells/uL, viral load undetectable for the past 6 years. The diagnostic challenge in this case is: (1) HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND) — even with undetectable plasma viral load, CNS viral replication and neuroinflammation can occur; (2) opportunistic infection (PML, cryptococcal meningitis, CMV encephalitis) must be excluded despite undetectable plasma viral load; (3) the behavioral syndrome (disinhibition, compulsive behavior, loss of empathy, stereotypy) is more consistent with bvFTD than typical HAND or HIV encephalopathy, which are more amnestic and attentional. The combination of frontally predominant behavioral syndrome and inadequate response to antidepressants in a woman in her mid-50s warrants full FTD evaluation.

results.title: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder vs bvFTD: neuroimaging and CSF biomarkers

output.summary: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND) in the ART era is typically characterized by: (1) attentional and processing speed deficits rather than behavioral disinhibition; (2) diffuse or subcortical FDG-PET changes (not focal frontotemporal); (3) CSF HIV RNA often detectable even with plasma suppression in HAND; (4) CSF NfL elevation present but the degree and pattern differ. bvFTD in HIV patients shows: (1) prominent behavioral disinhibition, perseveration, and social cognition loss; (2) frontotemporal FDG-PET hypometabolism with posterior preservation; (3) CSF HIV RNA undetectable in both plasma and CSF (when HAND is excluded). The presence of prominent behavioral disinhibition, compulsive behavior, and social cognition loss, in combination with focal frontotemporal metabolic changes, may help distinguish bvFTD from HAND in HIV-positive patients. Clinical correlation recommended.

interactions: Biktarvy + sertraline: minimal clinically significant interaction; sertraline CYP450 metabolism does not significantly interact with integrase-based ART

Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime: minimal ART interaction; useful for bvFTD behavioral disturbance and sleep
Low-dose sertraline continuation is appropriate for concurrent depression component

critical_actions: CSF JC PCR is MANDATORY in any HIV patient with new neurological or behavioral syndrome — PML requires CSF JC PCR for diagnosis (MRI can be negative early)
CSF HIV RNA (not just plasma) must be checked — plasma suppression does not guarantee CNS suppression in HAND
Antiretroviral therapy must NOT be interrupted — ART is essential and does not worsen FTD
contraindicated_actions: Discontinuing ART — this would allow HIV rebound and increase OI risk
key_reasoning_points: In HIV-positive patients with behavioral or cognitive syndrome, a complete CSF panel is essential: CSF HIV RNA (CNS compartment may differ from plasma), JC PCR (PML), cryptococcal antigen, and full OI panel — plasma suppression does not rule out CNS disease

HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND) in the ART era typically presents with ATTENTIONAL and processing speed deficits, not the behavioral disinhibition/perseveration/social cognition loss pattern of bvFTD

The FDG-PET pattern distinguishes: HAND shows diffuse or subcortical-frontal metabolism reduction; bvFTD shows focal frontotemporal hypometabolism with posterior preservation — these patterns are distinguishable
ART must be continued in HIV-positive bvFTD patients — there is no drug interaction concern with integrase-based regimens and standard FTD symptomatic medications
